feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 & 0 \\ 0 & 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: Notice that since ${A}^{T}\,A$ is diagonal, the singular values of $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\sigma }_{1}={\sigma }_{2}=\sqrt{20}.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$): Seeking non-zero solutions of $({A}^{T}\,A-20I)v=0,$ we obtain the unit eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{20}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{20}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{20}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{20}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U,$ $Σ,$ and $V:$ 

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{20} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{20}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
